title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Quantization, Prompt Sets, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the integrated process we use at Redwood Inference to onboard models into the eval harness, maintain prompt sets and benchmarks, certify quantization profiles, and run regression triage when quality regressions are detected. It is intended for ML engineers, SREs, and applied ML reviewers responsible for model serving and production quality.

Goals
- Ensure consistent, reproducible evals across model variants and quantization levels.
- Provide clear, time-bound procedures for triaging regressions and rolling back or remediating model variants.
- Maintain a curated prompt-set catalog that represents our common production task families.
- Define acceptance thresholds and sign-off criteria for quantized models.

Scope and ownership
- Scope: models entering Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private serving runtimes. Includes open-source model imports and internally packaged variants.
- Owners: Applied ML (primary), Serving Runtime (secondary), Applied ML Evals (process custodian).

High-level flow
1) Model onboarding into eval harness (owner: Applied ML).
2) Baseline prompt-set evaluation (owner: Applied ML Evals).
3) Quantization profile validation (owner: Quantization team / Applied ML).
4) Canary / rollout with monitoring and quality SLOs (owner: Serving Runtime + SRE).
5) Regression triage and rollback (owner: Applied ML + Incident Response).

Prompt set & benchmark guidelines
- Prompt-set taxonomy: classify prompts into families (instruction-following, code generation, summarization, retrieval-augmented QA, classification, conversational context).
- Minimum prompt-set size per family: 200 labeled examples for regression-sensitive families (e.g., instruction-following, summarization), 100 for lower-risk families.
- Metadata required for each prompt: id, family, description, expected_output_type, scoring_metric, tags, owner.

Prompt-set example (CSV columns)
- id, family, text, expected, metric, source, owner

Benchmarking metrics and acceptance thresholds
- Metrics we track per prompt family: ROUGE-L (summarization), BLEU (code/comment), Exact Match / F1 (QA), Perplexity (language modeling sanity check), BERTScore (semantic similarity), and human-evaluated quality for new models.
- Acceptance thresholds (typical, adjustable by product):
  - Instruction-following: human-quality pass rate >= 92% on a sampled eval (n=250) OR automated proxy (BERTScore >= 0.82 and no >2% drop on calibration prompts).
  - Summarization: ROUGE-L drop <= 1.5 points vs baseline, human regression rate < 3%.
  - Retrieval QA: F1 drop <= 2 points vs baseline.
  - Code generation: functional correctness on sampled unit tests >= 85%.

Quantization profile validation
- Profiles: per-model profiles live in quantization-profiles catalog; each profile includes: target precision (int8, int4), calibration dataset, calibration procedure, expected latency & memory gains, and known quality deltas vs FP16.
- Validation steps:
  1. Run full eval harness at FP16 to establish baseline metrics.
  2. Run quantized variant with same seed and prompt-set; collect automated metrics and sample outputs for human review.
  3. Compare metric deltas and run targeted human evaluation on top-k failing prompts (n=50-100).
  4. If automated metrics exceed configured thresholds, mark profile as "requires mitigation" and open an action ticket.

Quantization acceptance criteria (default)
- int8: automated metric deltas <= 1.5% relative or within family-specific absolute thresholds; human regression rate < 3% on sampled prompts.
- int4: allowed only for low-risk families or when latency/memory gains justify manual sign-off; automated metric deltas <= 3% and human regression rate < 5% unless product approves higher tolerance.

Regression detection & alerting
- Detection sources: nightly eval harness runs, canary production comparisons, user-reported incidents, AB test monitoring.
- Alerting rules (examples):
  - Trigger alert when any family-level metric drops more than configured delta for 3 consecutive nightly runs (default delta: 1.5% relative).
  - Trigger on spike in user error reports mapped to the serving route (>50 reports/day or doubling of baseline).

Triage playbook (step-by-step)
1. Acknowledge: Pager duty / Slack channel (applied-ml-evals) acknowledges within 1 hour.
2. Triage call (30 minutes): gather owner, serving runtime, SRE, product manager.
3. Data collection (owner: applied-ml-evals):
   - Pull nightly eval run artifacts (metrics, diffs, sample outputs) from the eval harness storage (S3 path pattern: s3://redwood-evals/<model>/<run_date>/).
   - Extract timeframe: last healthy baseline run and first failing run.
   - Collect production traces for affected routes (sampled tokens, latency, cold vs warm KV-cache counts).
4. Initial hypothesis generation: is regression correlated with quantization profile, code change (runtime), prompt-set update, or dataset drift?
5. Mitigation options (ordered by risk):
   - Hotfix: revert to prior model version or FP16 serving variant.
   - Partial rollback: route X% traffic away from new variant (canary rollback).
   - Patch: apply prompt engineering guardrail (e.g., prefix constraints) as short-term mitigation.
   - Long-term: retrain or adapt quantization calibration.
6. Action assignment & SLA: assign owner and target SLA for fix (critical regressions: 4 hours to mitigation; high-impact but non-critical: 48 hours).
7. Postmortem: create incident doc under applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage and link to the model page.

Runbook snippets and commands
- Trigger a full eval run (CI job) for a model variant:
  - CLI: ./scripts/run_eval_harness.sh --model-id rwd/model-name --prompt-set canonical --output s3://redwood-evals/rwd-model-name/latest --profile full

- Compare two runs (example Python snippet)
  - python tools/compare_runs.py --run-a s3://redwood-evals/rwd-model-a/2026-05-10 --run-b s3://redwood-evals/rwd-model-a/2026-05-24 --metrics ROUGE-L,BERTScore --out diff-report.json

Human evaluation protocol
- Sample selection: stratified by prompt family and by automated-failure-score (prioritize high-confidence failures). Default n=200 for initial sign-off, n=50 for targeted rechecks.
- Rater instructions: provide 3-point scale (better / same / worse) relative to baseline; capture free-text notes for recurring failure modes.
- Inter-rater agreement: Cohen's kappa target >= 0.6 before using new raters for production sign-off.

Rollout & canary guidance
- Canary stages: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with at least 24 hours at each stage for high-risk families, 12 hours for lower-risk families.
- Observability checks at each stage: prompt-family metric deltas, latency P95, token-level error spikes, user-reported feedback tags.
- Automatic rollback triggers: any critical metric crossing predefined threshold (example: human regression estimate > 5% or latency P95 increase > 50ms and > 20% relative).

Templates and artifacts to attach
- Eval run artifact naming convention: <model>-<variant>-<profile>-<YYYYMMDD>-run.json.gz
- Quantization profile template (YAML):

profile_name: rwd-gptq-int8
precision: int8
calibration_dataset: calibration/corpus-v2
calibration_method: per-channel-minmax
notes: "Expected perf: -1.2% ROUGE-L, latency -25%"
owner: applied-ml

- Regression incident template fields: incident_id, model_id, variant, quant_profile, detected_at, severity, primary_hypothesis, mitigation, incident_owner, postmortem_link

- Quantization profiles best practices: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026

Appendix: example failure modes and recommended mitigations
- Mode: hallucination increase after int8 quantization. Mitigation: increase calibration dataset diversity, use symmetric quantization for attention weights, or fallback to mixed FP16 kernel for attention layers.
- Mode: reduced factual precision on retrieval-augmented QA. Mitigation: adjust retrieval prompt templates, lock retrieval model version, enforce top-k reranking.

Contact and escalation
- Primary contact: applied-ml-evals@redwood.ai (pager: #applied-ml-evals).
- Escalation: if unresolved after SLA window, alert Eng SRE on-call and Product PM owner.
